transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Yeah, hi, Doctor. I guess… what finally pushed me to come in is I’ve been getting pulled off track by the tiniest things for maybe the past year or so. Like my phone buzzes once, or someone walks past my office, or I’ll be in the middle of something and suddenly I’m thinking about my in-laws for no reason—don’t get me started on them—and then I’m just off whatever I was doing before I even realize it. It’s been frustrating, especially with work.
When your mind gets pulled away like that, are the thoughts usually worries or fears about something bad happening, or are they just random unrelated thoughts?

Mostly they’re just random, not really like fear thoughts. It’ll be something tiny, like my phone buzzes or somebody walks past my office, and then I’m off on some other track before I can stop it. Or I’ll suddenly think about my in-laws—who, honestly, that could become a whole separate conversation—and then I realize I’m not doing the thing I was supposed to be doing anymore.

Thinking back, did you notice this kind of distractibility and difficulty staying on task when you were a kid or teenager, or is this really something that's only been happening in the last year or so?

Yeah, looking back, it wasn’t totally new. I mean, I didn’t think of it that way at the time, I was just “that kid,” you know? Teachers were always moving my seat because I’d talk too much, or I’d get up without asking, or I’d blurt something out before they even finished the question.  

And honestly, I remember one teacher putting me right next to her desk, which felt like prison at the time—though I probably deserved it. So yeah, I guess it was there when I was a kid too, not just this past year.
